scope: User-requested Cryer peak-time/loading-history review and follow-up plan, 2026-10-28 JST

current_loading_audit.source_clock_law: For Tr>0: q(t_n)=q0*min(max(t_n,0)/Tr,1); for Tr=0: q(t_n)=q0 including the first interaction.
current_loading_audit.predictor_corrector_clock: Both force stages read outer TimeStep=t_n; the member advances only after the full step. With positive Tr this nonautonomous-load timing warrants a separate order check; with current Tr=0 it does not change q.
current_loading_audit.initial_load_telemetry: Part0 is saved before first interaction, so its zero load diagnostic is not an implicit ramp. Sealed Part1/2 have nonzero confinement contributions on all 37173 soil IDs.
current_loading_audit.timing_conclusion: The lag spans roughly 8674 steps; one-stage clock timing cannot explain it, and there is no explicit nonzero ramp in these runs.
current_loading_audit.initial_condition_caveat: Native pressure initially equals zero; the instantaneous quasi-static step solution has internal p/q -> 1 at t -> 0+. Physical wave/build-up and initial-state compatibility remain separate hypotheses.

offline_linear_quasistatic_ramp_theory.definition: G_s(t) is the unit-step pressure response at fixed reference radius s=r/a. For Tr>0, p(t)/q0=(1/Tr)*integral_0^min(t,Tr) G_s(t-u) du.
offline_linear_quasistatic_ramp_theory.modal_evaluation: For G_s=sum a_n exp(-lambda_n*t), use sum a_n exp(-lambda_n*max(0,t-Tr))*(-expm1(-lambda_n*min(t,Tr)))/(lambda_n*Tr). lambda_n=xi_n^2*Cv/a^2. No shifted simulation times or interpolated native states.
offline_linear_quasistatic_ramp_theory.small_ramp_limit: For a smooth interior peak and Tr much shorter than the response time, the peak delay is approximately Tr/2; this is not a universal exact time correction.
offline_linear_quasistatic_ramp_theory.limitations: These are theoretical sensitivity calculations, not new SPH runs or evidence that the existing zero-ramp data experienced an 8-ms ramp. Peak optimizer last digits are not physical precision. The model is linear/quasi-static, not a dynamic numerical surrogate.

follow_up_order: Leave cryer_damp_peak_r1 running unchanged; complete and independently review the damping-only matched-time comparison first.

For any later finite-ramp experiment, declare the actual q(t), load-start/full-load/drainage event clocks and observation radius before running. Compare with the same-history convolution theory, not the old step curve or an empirically translated time axis.

Before interpreting finite-ramp Cryer results, check predictor/corrector external-load clock order using a bounded prescribed-force test. Any code correction requires CPU/GPU tests and preservation of existing Tr=0 regressions; no global TimeStep mutation or silent solver change.

If justified by completed damping and spatial-consistency evidence, select at most one positive binary ramp for an initial bounded coarse/half test; do not automatically launch a multi-case long matrix or choose Tr solely to align the old peak.

Separate a compatible preload/initial-state comparison from ramp duration: verify total stress, pressure, displacement and drainage compatibility before using a changed initial state. Do not simply assign p=q0 and claim an equivalent solution.

Report sampled peak time and native output cadence separately. Use matched actual times/material IDs and a distinct, clearly labelled peak-time estimator if needed; never alter retained raw clocks or existing acceptance limits.

Continue the initial-layout/zero-order force-consistency diagnosis in parallel. A ramp or damping change cannot by itself demonstrate that spatial consistency, peak amplitude and late decay are repaired.
